Masks stay attached when heads turn; a full backward look requires a torso pivot.

One immense PRIVATE ROYAL BEDCHAMBER, not a throne hall. NORTH: a raised platform with a luxurious burgundy Persian-textile BED, reached by one broad step. A level main floor runs 12 meters SOUTH from that platform to the NORTH stairs of a roughly six-meter-square sunken seating area. Exactly THREE broad shallow steps descend SOUTH into this lower square. The lower floor has thick carpets and perimeter cushions with clear standing/walking space; a narrow exposed stone strip borders the central carpet. Massive columns, bronze objects and cabinets surround the MAIN floor. EAST/WEST entrances near the NORTH bed zone connect to dark corridors. All real companions may move on the main floor and rim, never down onto ANY recess step or lower floor. Only Zahhak and named dream/prophecy bodies occupy the lower square. No extra people.

PLAN 04 | LIGHT AND EXPOSURE

DEEP NIGHT. Blackness is the dominant image, not a blue-lit room. The ONLY source is one fixed vertical cold silver-blue shaft through a small ceiling opening directly above the CENTER OF THE SUNKEN SQUARE. It lands on one isolated circular patch of the LOWER floor. Its edge is sharply contained; faint airborne dust describes the shaft only inside it. Never evenly expose the whole face or body. A turn can take that fragment back into black. Highlights belong to fixed world-space light, not the lens; no permanent eye catchlight, luminous eyes or light that tracks a face. Keep masks and skin unchanged. Emotional action stays legible through these fragments, movement and breath.

Preserve large areas of true black without shadow recovery or a uniform blue wash; only sparse highlights carry restrained silver-blue color. Dream and prophecy figures never reveal identifying facial planes, mask details or eyes, including in low angles. Their silhouettes come from the existing shaft or lit floor behind them, never a new backlight. No aura, energy effects or glowing outlines.

Character and location references control identity and construction, not their photographed brightness. The written lighting overrides any brighter reference. Each shot's LIGHTING instruction defines the visible fragment; everything else may remain black. Do not replace every shot with total black: the specified action-bearing detail must remain faintly readable.

START STATE AND BLOCKING

24mm from beside his head looking EAST at Warrior LEFT arriving at the EAST pool edge, facing WEST toward Zahhak. Hard cut beside Zahhak's other shoulder looking WEST at Warrior RIGHT arriving at WEST edge, facing EAST. This is Zahhak's explicit opposite eyeline, not a relocated actor. 50mm downward close from beside his support hand. Mace head stops on the stone strip SOUTH of Zahhak; he tightens his own staff grip, free hand rising into frame. One dry final scrape, then tense breathing. The three positions remain fixed for the next block.
